In monocot roots, water initially enters through root hairs and moves through the cortex via the apoplast and symplast pathways until it reaches the endodermis.  
The Casparian strip in the endodermis blocks the apoplastic pathway, forcing water and solutes to pass through the cytoplasm of endodermal cells before entering the vascular tissue.  
Thus, the first point where water must enter the cytoplasm of cells is at the endodermis.
